newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count up 17 to 825 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count up 17 to 825 in latest week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 825 as of September 20, up 17 from the prior week and 50 above the year-ago total of 775, Baker Hughes Inc reported.
The number of rigs drilling on land rose by 13 to 694, while rigs working offshore rose by six to 111. The number of rigs active in inland waters fell by two to 20.
The biggest change in individual states occurred in New Mexico, which showed an increase of seven and Texas, which rose by six. Oklahoma rose by five.

A total of 309 rigs were exploring for crude oil, up nine from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas rose by eight to 511, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained unchanged at five.
There were 187 rigs drilling directionally, 59 drilling horizontally and 579 drilling vertically.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by 19 to 259 versus 225 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
